examples.en: Fried tofu sushi is popular as a lunchbox item.
I ate udon with fried tofu in it.
I bought a bag of fried tofu pouches at the mart.
The fried tofu soaks up the broth, so it is delicious.
The child picks out only the fried tofu to eat.

examples.ko: 내일 점심에는 유부를 넣고 김밥을 말 거예요.
examples.en: For lunch tomorrow, I will roll gimbap with fried tofu in it.

explain: 한국에서는 '유부초밥', '유부우동'처럼 다른 음식 이름 안에 넣어 말하는 일이 많아요. 찌개나 부침에 넣는 '두부'와 쓰임이 달라서 둘을 바꿔 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: In Korea this word mostly shows up inside dish names like '유부초밥' and '유부우동'. It is used differently from plain '두부', which goes into stews and pan-fried dishes, so the two are not interchangeable.

examples.en: I have never seen a sunset this beautiful.
Why did you get up this early?

examples.ko: 그 사람이 이토록 화를 낼 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I did not know he would get this angry.
I have waited this long and still no one is coming.

examples.ko: 이토록 좋은 날씨에 집에만 있기 아까워요.
examples.en: It feels like a waste to stay home in weather this nice.

examples.ko: 이토록 많은 사람이 올 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I did not expect this many people to come.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '이렇게'를 더 많이 써요. '이토록'은 놀람이나 아쉬움 같은 감정이 담긴 글, 노래 가사, 소설에서 자주 보여요. 정도를 강조하는 말이라 뒤에 '아름다운', '오래'처럼 정도를 나타내는 말이 자주 와요.
explain_en: In everyday talk Koreans say '이렇게' much more often. '이토록' appears in writing, song lyrics, and novels, where it carries feelings such as surprise or regret. It emphasizes degree, so it is often followed by words of degree like '아름다운' or '오래'.

examples.en: Hot steam comes out of the kettle.

examples.ko: 욕실에 증기가 가득 차서 거울이 흐려졌어요.
examples.en: The bathroom filled with steam and the mirror fogged up.
In the old days, steam locomotives pulled the trains.
The dumplings cooked in steam are soft.

examples.ko: 다리미에서 증기가 나오면 옷이 잘 펴져요.
examples.en: When steam comes out of the iron, clothes smooth out well.
Be careful with the steam so you do not get burned.

explain: 일상에서는 '김'이라는 말을 더 자주 써요. '밥에서 김이 나요'처럼요. '증기'는 '증기 기관', '증기 다리미'처럼 기계나 과학 이야기에서 주로 써요.
explain_en: In daily life Koreans more often say '김', as in '밥에서 김이 나요'. '증기' shows up mainly in talk about machines and science, such as '증기 기관' and '증기 다리미'.

examples.en: This is a pristine area, so the air is clean.
This is seafood raised in pristine waters.
We have to protect Jeju Island's pristine nature.

examples.ko: 청정 에너지를 쓰는 차가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of cars that run on clean energy is growing.
We swam in a pristine mountain valley stream.
It is a fish that lives only in unpolluted water.

explain: 보통 '청정 지역', '청정 에너지'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여서 써요. 사람 손이 닿지 않은 깨끗함이라서, 방이나 옷이 깨끗하다고 할 때는 '깨끗하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It usually sits in front of another noun, as in '청정 지역' and '청정 에너지'. It means purity untouched by people, so for a clean room or clean clothes you say '깨끗하다' instead.

examples.en: These socks are made of nylon, so they are durable.
Nylon clothes dry fast, so they are convenient.
I tied the tent with a nylon rope.
Nylon shirts are a bit hot in summer.
Fishing line is usually nylon.
It is a nylon bag, so it is fine even in the rain.

explain: '면'은 식물, '울'은 양털에서 얻고 나일론은 공장에서 만든 섬유라서 가볍고 빨리 말라요. 한국에서는 '나일론 양말', '나일론 줄'처럼 옷감이나 재료 이름 앞에 붙여 자주 써요.
explain_en: '면' comes from plants and '울' from sheep, while 나일론 is a factory-made fiber that is light and dries quickly. In Korean it often comes before the item, as in '나일론 양말' and '나일론 줄'.

examples.en: The teacher read the poem aloud slowly.
At the graduation ceremony, a student representative reads a letter aloud.
I read a storybook aloud to my child.
I am embarrassed to read my diary aloud in front of a friend.

examples.ko: 내일 수업 시간에 이 글을 낭독할 거예요.
examples.en: I will read this piece aloud in class tomorrow.
I like the voice that reads listeners' stories aloud on the radio.

explain: '읽다'는 눈으로만 읽어도 되지만 '낭독하다'는 여러 사람 앞에서 소리 내어 읽을 때 써요. 시, 편지, 선언문처럼 격식 있는 글과 잘 어울려요. 편하게 말할 때는 '소리 내어 읽다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '읽다' can mean reading silently, but '낭독하다' means reading out loud in front of others. It suits formal pieces such as poems, letters, and declarations. In casual speech people say '소리 내어 읽다'.

examples.en: Yellow dandelions have bloomed by the roadside.
Dandelion seeds fly away in the wind.
My grandmother made dandelion greens for me.
I picked a dandelion on the lawn.
When spring comes, dandelions appear everywhere.
I want to live tenaciously like a dandelion.

explain: 하얗게 둥근 씨앗 뭉치는 '민들레 홀씨'라고 해요. 아무 데서나 잘 자라서 동요나 시에서는 끈질기게 사는 사람을 민들레에 비유해요. 잎은 나물로도 먹어요.
explain_en: The round white puff of seeds is called '민들레 홀씨'. Because it grows almost anywhere, children's songs and poems compare tough, persistent people to a dandelion. The leaves are also eaten as '나물'.

examples.en: I read the book's preface first.
The author wrote words of thanks in the preface.
The preface is long, so it takes a while to reach the main text.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 서문 없이 바로 시작해요.
examples.en: This novel starts right away with no preface.
Writing the preface was hard, so I worried over it for days.
The translated edition has a preface written by the translator.

explain: 같은 뜻으로 '머리말'도 많이 써요. 저자가 쓴 앞글은 '서문', 다른 사람이 책을 소개하며 쓴 글은 '추천사'예요. 책 끝에 붙이는 글은 '후기'나 '맺음말'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '머리말' is a common synonym. A preface by the author is '서문', while a piece by someone else recommending the book is '추천사'. A note at the end of a book is called '후기' or '맺음말'.

examples.en: The boat leaves from the dock.
It takes thirty minutes by bus to get to the dock.
I had grilled fish at a restaurant in front of the dock.
Anglers are gathered at the dock.
It rained, so the dock is slippery.

examples.ko: 섬에 가려면 이 선착장에서 표를 사야 해요.
examples.en: To go to the island, you have to buy a ticket at this dock.

explain: '항구'는 큰 배가 드나드는 넓은 곳이고, '선착장'은 작은 배나 여객선이 서는 곳이에요. 섬에 갈 때 자주 듣는 말이에요. '부두'는 짐을 싣는 곳이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: '항구' is a large harbor for big ships, while '선착장' is where small boats and passenger ferries stop. You hear it often when going to an island. '부두' feels more like a place for loading cargo.

examples.en: The river water makes a whirlpool, spinning round and round.
When I poured milk into the coffee, a swirl formed.
The boat nearly got sucked into the whirlpool.
The sink water swirls as it goes down.
That matter grew into a big turmoil.

examples.ko: 마음속에 소용돌이가 일어서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: Turmoil rose inside me, so I could not sleep.

explain: 물이나 바람이 빙글빙글 도는 모양 말고, '혼란의 소용돌이', '논란의 소용돌이'처럼 큰 혼란을 비유할 때도 많이 써요. 동사 '소용돌이치다'로도 써요.

phrases.en: get swept up in the turmoil of an incident
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 사건이나 혼란에 얽혀 빠져나오기 어렵다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Being pulled into a big event or confusion and finding it hard to get out.
phrases.en_equiv: get caught up in a whirlwind

explain_en: Besides spinning water or wind, it is often used figuratively for big turmoil, as in '혼란의 소용돌이' and '논란의 소용돌이'. There is also the verb '소용돌이치다'.

examples.en: This speaker is stereo, so the sound feels three-dimensional.
The song sounds rich when I listen in stereo.
I watched a movie with stereo earphones.
In the old days, every living room had a big stereo.

examples.ko: 왼쪽과 오른쪽 소리가 다른 게 스테레오예요.
examples.en: When the left and right sounds differ, that is stereo.
It is a stereo recording, so you can feel where each instrument is.

explain: 한쪽에서만 소리가 나는 '모노'의 반대로, 왼쪽과 오른쪽이 다르게 나오는 소리를 말해요. 오디오 기계 자체를 '스테레오'라고 부르기도 하지만 요즘은 '스피커', '오디오'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '모노', where one channel carries all the sound; in stereo the left and right sides differ. Some people call the audio machine itself a '스테레오', but today '스피커' and '오디오' are more common.

examples.en: The jockey holds a whip and drives the horse.
At the circus, the trainer cracked a whip.
At the sound of the whip, the ox quickened its pace.

examples.ko: 옛날 영화에서 채찍을 쓰는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: There is a scene in an old movie where someone uses a whip.
Whipping scenes are scary for a child to watch.

examples.ko: 그 말은 저에게 큰 채찍이 되었어요.
examples.en: Those words became a big spur for me.

explain: '당근과 채찍'은 상과 벌을 같이 쓴다는 뜻으로 자주 나와요. '채찍질하다'는 진짜 때리는 것뿐 아니라 '스스로를 채찍질하다'처럼 더 열심히 하도록 몰아붙인다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.example: 좋은 팀장은 당근과 채찍을 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칭찬이나 상과 벌을 함께 써서 사람을 움직인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using praise or rewards together with punishment to motivate people.

phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로를 더 열심히 하도록 몰아붙인다는 뜻이에요.

explain_en: '당근과 채찍' often appears to mean using rewards and punishment together. '채찍질하다' can mean actually whipping, but also pushing hard to work harder, as in '스스로를 채찍질하다'.

examples.en: The ship leaves port at seven in the morning.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 어제는 배가 출항하지 못했어요.
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, the ship could not leave port yesterday.
The fishermen set out to sea at dawn.
I waved at the ship that was leaving port.
If the weather clears up, we will set sail tomorrow.
The cruise ship leaves port in Busan and goes to Japan.

explain: '출항하다'는 배에만 써요. 비행기가 떠날 때는 '이륙하다', 버스나 기차는 '출발하다'를 써요. 반대로 배가 항구에 들어오는 것은 '입항하다'예요.
explain_en: '출항하다' is used only for ships. A plane taking off is '이륙하다', and buses and trains use '출발하다'. The opposite, a ship entering a harbor, is '입항하다'.

examples.en: The ship slowly passes through the narrow strait.
I can see a small island across the strait.

examples.ko: 한국과 일본 사이에는 넓은 해협이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a wide strait between Korea and Japan.
The wind is strong in the strait, so the waves are high.

examples.ko: 다리를 놓아서 해협을 차로 건널 수 있어요.
examples.en: A bridge was built, so you can cross the strait by car.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 해협을 건너는 배가 자주 취소돼요.
examples.en: In winter, ferries crossing the strait are often cancelled.

explain: '대한해협', '도버 해협'처럼 지명 뒤에 붙여 써요. '바다'보다 좁고 양쪽에 땅이 가까운 느낌이에요. 뉴스나 지리 시간에는 자주 나오지만 일상 대화에서는 드물어요.
explain_en: It attaches after place names, as in '대한해협' and '도버 해협'. It feels narrower than '바다', with land close on both sides. It is common in news and geography class but rare in everyday talk.

examples.ko: 올해 후반기에는 여행을 많이 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I plan to travel a lot in the second half of this year.
Now that it is the second half, work has gotten much busier.

examples.ko: 야구 시즌 후반기에 우리 팀이 강해졌어요.
examples.en: Our team got stronger in the second half of the baseball season.
Classes for the second half start in September.

examples.ko: 회사는 후반기 계획을 다시 짜고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is redoing its plans for the second half.
The further into the second half of the season, the more intense the games get.

explain: 한 해나 시즌, 학기를 반으로 나눈 뒤쪽이에요. 앞쪽은 '전반기'예요. 경기 하나의 뒷부분은 '후반전'이라고 하고, 한 해에서는 '하반기'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the latter half of a year, season, or semester. The first half is '전반기'. The second part of a single game is '후반전', and for a year '하반기' is also common.

en: start a semester; start a course

examples.en: Universities start the semester in early March.

examples.ko: 다음 주에 영어 수업이 개강해서 바빠요.
examples.en: The English course starts next week, so I am busy.
The new class at the academy started on Monday.
I bought the textbook before the course started.

examples.ko: 방학이 끝나고 개강할 때가 되니 아쉬워요.
examples.en: Now that the break is over and school is about to start, I feel sad.
I heard the semester starts in the first week of September.

explain: 학교나 학원에서 새 학기나 새 강좌가 시작될 때 써요. 반대로 학기가 끝나는 것은 '종강하다'예요. 학생들은 '개강 첫날'처럼 명사로도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when a new semester or course begins at a school or academy. The opposite, the end of a term, is '종강하다'. Students also use the noun form, as in '개강 첫날'.

examples.en: The employer has to pay wages on time.
The new employer is kind to the staff.
The employer and the employee wrote up a contract.

examples.ko: 그는 고용주를 잘 만나서 일이 편해요.
examples.en: He got a good employer, so his work is easy.

examples.ko: 고용주가 바뀌면 근무 조건도 달라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the employer changes, working conditions can change too.

examples.ko: 외국인 직원의 고용주는 비자 서류를 준비해야 해요.
examples.en: The employer of a foreign worker has to prepare the visa documents.

explain: 일하는 사람은 '근로자'나 '직원'이에요. 일상에서는 보통 '사장님'이라고 부르고, '고용주'는 법, 계약, 뉴스에서 쓰는 말이에요. 사람을 직접 부를 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: The other side is '근로자' or '직원'. In daily life people say '사장님', and '고용주' belongs to law, contracts, and news. You never use it to address someone directly.

examples.ko: 우리 팀 공격수가 두 골을 넣었어요.
examples.en: Our team's forward scored two goals.
He is a forward famous for his speed.

examples.ko: 공격수가 공을 몰고 골문 앞까지 뛰었어요.
examples.en: The forward dribbled the ball and ran up to the goal.

examples.ko: 새 공격수가 팀에 들어와서 분위기가 좋아요.
examples.en: A new forward joined the team, so the mood is good.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때 공격수로 뛰고 싶었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I wanted to play as a forward.

examples.ko: 공격수는 수비수보다 골을 넣을 기회가 많아요.
examples.en: Forwards have more chances to score than defenders.

explain: 축구 같은 단체 경기에서 공격을 맡은 선수를 말해요. 반대는 '수비수'예요. 축구에서는 '스트라이커'라는 말도 쓰고, 야구에서 공격하는 선수는 '타자'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a player in charge of attacking in team games such as soccer. The opposite is '수비수'. In soccer people also say '스트라이커', and in baseball the attacking player is a '타자'.

examples.en: There are many bridges over the Han River.
The new bridge is scheduled to be completed next year.
The road is jammed because of the bridge construction.

examples.ko: 오래된 교량은 안전 점검을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Old bridges need safety inspections.
Once you cross this bridge, you are right in the city.

examples.ko: 밤이 되면 교량들은 조명이 켜져서 예뻐요.
examples.en: At night the bridges are lit up and look pretty.

explain: 일상에서는 '다리'가 훨씬 흔해요. '교량'은 공사, 뉴스, 안내문에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 사람이나 일이 둘 사이를 이어 줄 때 '교량 역할'이라고 비유해서도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 통역사가 두 회사의 교량 역할을 해요.
phrases.en: serve as a bridge between two sides
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 둘을 이어 주는 사람이나 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person or thing that connects two different sides.

explain_en: In daily life '다리' is far more common. '교량' is the formal word used in construction, news, and notices. It is also used figuratively, as in '교량 역할', for someone or something that connects two sides.

examples.ko: 이 도로는 군용 차량이 자주 다녀요.
examples.en: Military vehicles often travel on this road.

examples.ko: 군용 시설 근처에서는 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos near military facilities.
A military plane passed through the sky.
Military blankets are thick and warm.
It was originally made for military use, so the watch is sturdy.

examples.ko: 이 땅은 군용지라서 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: This land is military land, so you cannot go in.

explain: '군용 차', '군용 담요'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여서 써요. 반대로 군대가 아닌 일반 사람이 쓰는 것은 '민간용'이라고 해요. 혼자 쓰이는 일은 드물어요.
explain_en: It goes in front of another noun, as in '군용 차' and '군용 담요'. For things used by ordinary people rather than the military, you say '민간용'. It rarely stands on its own.

examples.en: This novel is that writer's best-known work.
I have seen all of that director's best-known films.
The Mona Lisa is Leonardo da Vinci's most famous work.

examples.ko: 대표작이 하나만 있어도 유명해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even a single signature work can make you famous.
Which song is that singer's signature work?
At the exhibition, I saw the painter's major works in one place.

explain: '대표작으로 꼽히다'처럼 자주 써요. '명작'은 훌륭하다고 인정받는 작품이라서 대표작과 꼭 같지 않아요. 대표작은 가장 잘 알려진 작품이라는 점이 기준이에요.
explain_en: It often appears in the pattern '대표작으로 꼽히다'. '명작' means a work recognized as excellent, so it is not always the same as 대표작; a 대표작 is judged by being the best known.

examples.en: In art class, we made a mosaic from colored paper.
There is a beautiful mosaic on the cathedral wall.
On the broadcast, they covered the face with pixelation.
I pixelated the license plate in the photo.

examples.ko: 작은 타일을 붙여 모자이크 그림을 완성했어요.
examples.en: We finished a mosaic picture by sticking on small tiles.
There is a mosaic-like pattern on the floor.

explain: 작은 조각을 붙여 만든 그림 말고도, 한국에서는 영상이나 사진의 일부를 네모 모양으로 흐리게 가리는 것도 '모자이크'라고 해요. '모자이크하다', '모자이크 처리하다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: blur out (a part of an image)
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상이나 사진에서 얼굴, 번호 같은 부분을 알아볼 수 없게 가린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Hiding parts such as faces or numbers in an image so they cannot be recognized.

explain_en: Besides a picture made of small pieces, Koreans also call blurring part of a photo or video into blocks '모자이크'. People say '모자이크하다' or '모자이크 처리하다' for this.

examples.en: A student representative read the declaration.
We learn about the declaration of independence in history class.

examples.ko: 환경 단체가 지구를 지키자는 선언문을 발표했어요.
examples.en: An environmental group released a declaration urging people to protect the Earth.
Those who agree with the declaration, please write your name.

examples.ko: 동아리 선언문을 모두 함께 소리 내어 읽었어요.
examples.en: We all read the club's declaration aloud together.
The declaration is short but powerful.

explain: '독립 선언문', '인권 선언문'처럼 중요한 약속이나 주장을 공식적으로 밝힐 때 써요. 개인의 다짐은 '다짐'이나 '각오'를 더 자주 써요. '성명서'는 입장을 알리는 글이라서 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It is used for formally stating an important promise or claim, as in '독립 선언문' and '인권 선언문'. For personal resolutions people say '다짐' or '각오'. '성명서' is a statement of a position, so it differs slightly.

examples.en: Our team's defender cleared the ball.

examples.ko: 수비수는 골대 앞에서 상대를 막아야 해요.
examples.en: A defender has to stop the opponents in front of the goal.

examples.ko: 키가 큰 수비수가 헤딩으로 골을 막았어요.
examples.en: A tall defender blocked the goal with a header.
The defender made a mistake and we gave up a goal.
I like forwards better than defenders.
I heard the new defender is very fast.

explain: 주로 축구에서 쓰는 말이에요. 반대는 '공격수'이고, 포지션 이름으로는 '센터백', '풀백'이 있어요. 야구에서는 수비하는 선수를 '야수'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is used mainly in soccer. The opposite is '공격수', and position names include '센터백' and '풀백'. In baseball, fielders are called '야수'.

examples.en: My mom was sick, so I ran the errand for her.
The child went to the shop to run an errand.

examples.ko: 동생은 심부름하고 받은 용돈으로 과자를 샀어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling bought snacks with the allowance earned from running an errand.

examples.ko: 회사에서 신입이 심부름해야 하는 일이 많아요.
examples.en: At work, a new hire has many errands to run.
I will run the errands today, so please rest.
I gave a snack to the child who was running the errand.

explain: 대부분 '심부름을 가다', '심부름을 시키다'처럼 말해요. 심부름을 하는 사람은 '심부름꾼'이에요. 아이 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 어른끼리는 '부탁'이나 '잡일'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Usually it appears as '심부름을 가다' or '심부름을 시키다'. A person who does errands is a '심부름꾼'. It comes up a lot in stories about children; adults say '부탁' or '잡일' instead.

examples.en: Jeju Island is mild even in winter.
Tangerines grow well in a mild climate.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 온난해서 눈이 거의 안 와요.
examples.en: This region is mild, so it hardly ever snows.

examples.ko: 남쪽 바다 근처는 비교적 온난할 거예요.
examples.en: Near the southern sea it should be relatively mild.
Thanks to the mild weather, it was great for a walk.
If the Earth gets warmer, sea levels rise.

explain: '따뜻하다'는 몸, 방, 음식에도 쓰지만 '온난하다'는 날씨, 기후, 지역에만 써요. 일기 예보나 지리 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '지구 온난화'라는 말로 더 자주 들어요.
explain_en: '따뜻하다' works for bodies, rooms, and food, but '온난하다' is only for weather, climate, and regions. It appears in forecasts and geography. You will most often hear it in '지구 온난화'.

examples.en: I had my initials engraved on the bag.
Please write just the initials of your name first.

examples.ko: 이니셜이 같은 사람이 반에 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are two people in my class with the same initials.
I signed with my English initials.
I embroidered my initials on a handkerchief.
The article showed only initials instead of the name.

explain: 영어 이름의 첫 글자를 말할 때가 많아요. 한글 이름의 첫 자음은 '초성'이라고 하고, 'ㄱㄷㅈ'처럼 자음만 써요. 뉴스에서 실명을 숨길 때 'K씨'처럼 이니셜을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It mostly means the first letters of a name written in the Roman alphabet. For Korean names, the first consonants are called '초성', written as consonants only like 'ㄱㄷㅈ'. News articles sometimes hide real names with initials, as in 'K씨'.

examples.ko: 여름에는 물놀이 중 익사 사고가 늘어요.
examples.en: In summer, drowning accidents during water play increase.

examples.ko: 구명조끼를 입으면 익사를 막을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Wearing a life jacket can prevent drowning.

examples.ko: 아이들 익사 사고가 없도록 어른이 지켜봐야 해요.
examples.en: Adults must watch so that children do not have drowning accidents.
A report of a drowning came on the news.

examples.ko: 익사 위험이 있어서 수영장에 안전 요원이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a risk of drowning, so the pool has lifeguards.
Fortunately, he was rescued just before drowning.

explain: 보통 '익사 사고', '익사 위험'처럼 다른 말과 붙여 써요. 물에 빠졌다가 살았을 때는 '물에 빠지다'를 쓰고, 숨졌을 때 '익사'를 써요. 뉴스와 안전 안내에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is usually combined with other words, as in '익사 사고' and '익사 위험'. If someone fell in the water but survived, say '물에 빠지다'; '익사' means they died. It is common in news and safety notices.

examples.ko: 작은 배가 뒤집혀서 두 명이 익사했어요.
examples.en: A small boat capsized and two people drowned.
I am afraid of water and worry that I might drown.

examples.ko: 수영을 못하는 사람은 깊은 물에서 익사하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: People who cannot swim easily drown in deep water.

examples.ko: 바다에서 익사하는 사고는 파도가 높을 때 많아요.
examples.en: Drownings at sea happen often when the waves are high.
He drowned before the rescue team arrived.
In the movie, the hero saves a drowning person.

explain: '물에 빠지다'는 살 수도 있지만 '익사하다'는 물에 빠져 목숨을 잃었다는 뜻이라 뉴스와 사고 기사에서 써요. 가까운 사람의 일을 말할 때는 보통 '사고로 돌아가셨다'처럼 돌려 말해요.
explain_en: '물에 빠지다' can end with survival, but '익사하다' means someone died in the water, so it appears in news and accident reports. For someone close, people usually soften it with '사고로 돌아가셨다'.

examples.en: Mom keeps urging us to hurry out.

examples.ko: 너무 재촉하지 마세요. 거의 다 했어요.
examples.en: Please do not rush me so much. I am almost done.
The customer kept hurrying the food, so the staff was busy.

examples.ko: 친구가 대답을 재촉하는 바람에 마음이 급했어요.
examples.en: My friend pressed me for an answer, so I felt rushed.
The landlord urged me to pay the rent.
The more you urge a child to hurry, the slower the child gets.

explain: 상대에게 빨리하라고 압박할 때 써요. 말투가 조금 부담스럽게 들릴 수 있어요. 부드럽게 말할 때는 '서둘러 주세요'가 좋아요. '독촉하다'는 돈이나 일을 내라고 계속 요구할 때 주로 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you press someone to be quick, and it can sound a bit pushy. For a softer request, '서둘러 주세요' works better. '독촉하다' is mostly for repeatedly demanding money or work.

examples.en: Labor pains started because the baby was about to come.

examples.ko: 진통이 오 분마다 와서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: The contractions came every five minutes, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 긴 진통 끝에 건강한 아기가 태어났어요.
examples.en: After long labor, a healthy baby was born.

examples.ko: 진통이 심해서 밤새 한숨도 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The pain was so bad that I did not sleep a wink all night.
I took a painkiller because of a headache.

examples.ko: 회사가 구조 개편을 하면서 진통이 컸어요.
examples.en: The company went through big growing pains during the restructuring.

explain: 아기를 낳기 전에 배가 아픈 것은 '진통', 아픔을 줄이는 약은 '진통제'예요. 어려운 일을 해내는 동안 겪는 갈등과 고통도 '진통을 겪다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 새 제도가 자리 잡기까지 진통을 겪었어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 일이 자리 잡을 때까지 갈등이나 어려움이 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Facing conflict and difficulty until something new settles in.

explain_en: The pain before childbirth is '진통', and the medicine that eases pain is '진통제'. The struggle and friction while getting through something hard is also '진통을 겪다'.

examples.en: Listening to the radio is my habit on the way to work.
The English listening test was hard.
If you send in a listener's story, they give you a gift.
I listen to the news every day as listening practice.
This program's audience ratings have risen a lot.
The recording was so fast that it was hard to follow.

explain: 일상에서는 '듣기'가 더 자연스러워요. '청취'는 방송이나 시험, 행사처럼 격식 있는 곳에서 써요. '청취자', '청취율'처럼 합쳐서 자주 말해요.
explain_en: In daily speech '듣기' sounds more natural. '청취' belongs to broadcasts, tests, and events. It often combines into other words such as '청취자' and '청취율'.

examples.en: I listen to the news on the radio every morning.
A session to hear citizens' opinions will be held.
At the meeting, we heard out the employees' complaints.

examples.ko: 음악을 청취하며 공부하면 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: If I study while listening to music, I cannot concentrate.
People who listened to the broadcast sent in their stories.
Tomorrow we will hear the expert's explanation.

explain: '듣다'보다 격식 있는 말이라서 방송, 회의, 공청회에서 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '듣다'를 쓰면 돼요. 기관이나 윗사람이 '의견을 청취하다'처럼 사람들의 말을 들을 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '듣다' and is used for broadcasts, meetings, and public hearings. In daily conversation just use '듣다'. Organizations and officials often use it, as in '의견을 청취하다'.

examples.ko: 광고주가 새 광고를 마음에 들어 했어요.
examples.en: The advertiser liked the new ad.
The advertiser changed, so the ad content changed too.
The broadcaster is busy looking for advertisers.
The advertiser made many requests, so the work was delayed.
I sent a results report to the advertiser.
YouTubers sign with advertisers and then film videos.

explain: 광고를 만드는 곳은 '광고 회사'이고, 광고비를 내고 맡기는 쪽이 '광고주'예요. '고객'이나 '클라이언트'라고도 하지만 광고 업계에서는 '광고주'가 기본이에요.
explain_en: The company that makes ads is a '광고 회사', and the side that pays and commissions them is the '광고주'. People also say '고객' or '클라이언트', but in the ad industry '광고주' is the standard word.

examples.ko: 이 휴대폰은 너무 구식이라 앱이 안 돼요.
examples.en: This phone is so outdated that apps do not work.
My grandmother's house has an old-style TV.
It is an old-style building, but the atmosphere is nice.

examples.ko: 그 생각은 요즘 보면 좀 구식이에요.
examples.en: That idea looks a bit old-fashioned these days.
My father still uses an old-style camera.

examples.ko: 구식 방법으로 만든 빵이라 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: The bread is made the old-fashioned way, so it tastes better.

explain: 반대말은 '신식'이에요. 기계나 방법이 오래돼서 요즘과 다를 때 쓰고, 사람에게 쓰면 생각이 낡았다는 느낌이라 실례가 될 수 있어요. '낡다'는 물건이 닳았다는 뜻이라 달라요.
explain_en: The opposite is '신식'. It is used for machines or methods that are old and different from today's. Applied to a person it implies outdated thinking and can be rude. '낡다' is different, meaning something is worn out.

examples.ko: 이 책은 국문과 영문이 같이 있어요.
examples.en: This book has both Korean and English text.
I have to change my Korean résumé into English.
I want to major in Korean literature at university.

examples.ko: 국문 제목을 먼저 쓰고 영문 제목을 쓰세요.
examples.en: Write the Korean title first, then the English title.
Please fill out the application in Korean.
There are not enough materials written in Korean.

explain: 한국어로 쓴 글을 말할 때 써요. 영어 글은 '영문'이라고 해서 서류에서 짝으로 자주 나와요. 그냥 말할 때는 '한국어'라고 해요. '국문학'은 한국어로 쓴 문학을 공부하는 학문이에요.
explain_en: It refers to writing done in Korean, and it pairs with '영문' for English text, often on forms and documents. In plain speech Koreans just say '한국어'. '국문학' is the study of literature written in Korean.

examples.ko: 이사 가기 전에 도배를 새로 했어요.
examples.en: I had the walls newly papered before moving.
After wallpapering, there is a smell of paste.

examples.ko: 벽지 값보다 도배 비용이 더 비싸요.
examples.en: The wallpapering cost is higher than the price of the wallpaper.
After the wallpapering was done, the room brightened up.

examples.ko: 도배 기술자가 하루 만에 방을 끝냈어요.
examples.en: The wallpapering worker finished the room in one day.
Mold has formed, so the walls need new wallpaper.

explain: '도배'는 '벽지', '장판'과 함께 집 공사 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 인터넷에서 같은 글을 계속 올리는 것도 '도배'라고 해서, 앞뒤 말을 보고 구분해요.
explain_en: '도배' often appears alongside '벽지' and '장판' when talking about home renovation. Posting the same message over and over online is also called '도배', so tell them apart from the context.

examples.en: I wallpapered the room myself over the weekend.

examples.ko: 벽을 도배하려면 먼저 낡은 벽지를 떼야 해요.
examples.en: To wallpaper a wall, you first have to peel off the old wallpaper.

examples.ko: 도배한 지 얼마 안 돼서 방이 깨끗해요.
examples.en: It has not been long since the wallpapering, so the room is clean.
My father wallpapered the living room by himself.

examples.ko: 이사 오기 전에 집을 도배해 놓았어요.
examples.en: I had the house wallpapered before moving in.

examples.ko: 내일 집을 도배할 사람이 오기로 했어요.
examples.en: The person who will wallpaper the house is coming tomorrow.

explain: 벽은 '도배하다', 바닥은 '장판을 깔다'라고 말해요. 같이 쓰는 말은 '벽지', '풀'이에요. 인터넷에서는 글이나 댓글을 계속 올려 화면을 가득 채우는 것도 '도배하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 누가 같은 광고 글로 게시판을 도배했어요.
phrases.en: flood a bulletin board with the same posts
phrases.nuance_ko: 인터넷에서 같은 글이나 댓글을 계속 올려 화면을 가득 채운다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Filling a page online by posting the same message or comments repeatedly.

explain_en: Walls are '도배하다' and floors are '장판을 깔다'. Related words are '벽지' and '풀'. Online, filling a page by posting the same posts or comments over and over is also '도배하다'.
